messages:
alex: :rotating_light: Noticing a throughput drop in eu-west-1 Dedicated pool around 12:30 UTC — p95 up, throughput down ~40%, several workers restarted with exit code 137.
maria: copy. Any OOM logs? Where's the trace? :eyes:
alex: attaching quick logs:
```
[2026-02-18T12:30:12Z] worker-17 ERROR GPU OOM (code 137)
[2026-02-18T12:30:12Z] runtime: unload kv cache shard 4 -> eviction triggered
[2026-02-18T12:30:13Z] worker-17 restart backoff 2s -> restart
```
jonathan: looking at profiler: kernel selection fell back to non-tuned matmul for long sequences; combined with large batches CV memory spiking. KV cache churn is high.
priya: noticed high KV eviction rate in metrics: kv_cache_evictions/s spiked from 0.4 to 12.7. Also batch size distribution shifted — more 64+ tokens per request.
deploy-bot: Automated alert: rolling restart started for pool dedicated-eu-west-1 at 12:35 UTC.
alex: also saw fragmentation counters increase; physical free decreased though overall usage not that high — suggests fragmentation after repeated allocations.
jonathan: hypothesis: batching heuristic allowed large batches because QPS suddenly higher; runtime chose a kernel variant that uses more temp buffers; combined with kv cache eviction and allocator fragmentation -> OOM.
maria: can we reproduce on staging with the same trace? If yes, test bumping preallocated arena size to reduce fragmentation.
priya: quick repro steps: replay request sample set (trace-id: tr-20260218-8f3) to a single worker with continuous batching enabled; observed identical OOM in 3/5 runs.
alex: quick mitigation applied: lowered max_batch_size from 48 -> 32 and disabled continuous batching window from 20ms -> 5ms. early results: throughput recovered to ~92% and no OOMs in 10m.
jonathan: longer-term fixes: (1) add kernel selection guard to avoid high-temp-buffer kernels when kv_evictions > threshold (2) pre-allocate KV cache slab to avoid per-request allocations (3) improve allocator defragmentation.
maria: assigned jonathan + priya to a postmortem. jonathan to own runtime patch, priya to own KV prealloc and tests. follow-up doc by EOD.
sre-oncall: monitoring alerts adjusted to detect kv_eviction spikes + kernel fallback events; added playbook: if kv_evictions/s > 5 and OOMs > 1 => throttle batch size and escalate.
alex: thanks all. saving trace and profile to https://redwood-internal/trace/tr-20260218-8f3 :white_check_mark:
